correctness.rationale: For R=1 the horizontal chord cut from the square of half-width sqrt(1-z²) changes at c|z|=(a±b)sqrt(1-z²). The Jacobian is 1/sqrt(a²+b²); the algebraic terms at the two thresholds cancel, yielding the inverse-tangent formula and its stated axis limits. At fixed c the area is four times the centered interval mean of a strictly convex derivative; pairing symmetric points shows strict increase with the interval radius 2ab, including the integrable c=0 limit. The sign of D' is the sign of g; differentiating arctan x−3x/(x²+3) proves g'>0, and the limits −4 and 4/3 prove one strict profile minimum and the maximum at k=0. Inclusion of the ball proves the lower bound, with strict excess in every other plane by an open set of radial directions with xy≠0. Independently split polar quadrature at the active-cylinder switch for seven normals, including coordinate boundaries, agreed with the formula to 10⁻⁴⁷ at 50-digit precision; the stationary value was independently 3.8203968413887654300 at k=1.3201367133766767181. This is numerical corroboration only; the universal check is RESULT.md lines 40–96. Frozen verify.py lines 13–80 and VERIFICATION.md describe a separate finite quadrature check; the source script was inspected, not executed.
